item.title: Why New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani wants 15% of whatever NYU’s new quantum lab invents
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has committed $29.2 million to NYU's Quantum Fabrication Facility (QFab) in Manhattan, set to open in 2030. In return, the city gets 15% of NYU's proceeds from intellectual property created with city-funded tools, plus three advisory board seats. Backed by $284 million in total funding, the new quantum lab will train CUNY students and support more than 100 companies.

item.title: Tyler Perry turned 330-acre former Army base into major Atlanta film studio
item.description: In 2015, Tyler Perry acquired the former Fort McPherson Army base in Atlanta for $30 million, and transformed it into a major production hub featuring 12 sound stages. This initiative not only aims to create new jobs but also emphasizes the importance of preserving historical structures while meeting the evolving demands of the film industry. Perry’s vision includes nurturing local talent to foster growth in South Atlanta's creative landscape.

item.title: US temple attack plot: Teen’s alleged manifesto describes Indians as ‘subhumans’
item.description: A 19-year-old white supremacist's intention to attack a temple near Chicago was disrupted by a rifle malfunction. Following the incident, concerned colleagues notified authorities after he expressed his intentions via messages. Police arrested Alexandros Paporakis, uncovering alarming materials including a manifesto that targeted several communities. The case has raised serious safety concerns among Hindu organizations about worship places.

item.title: Elvis Presley bought Beverly Hills home for $400,000; it later sold for $25.5m
item.description: In 1967, Elvis and Priscilla Presley acquired an opulent home in Beverly Hills' Trousdale Estates for $400,000. Their tenure at the estate lasted until 1973, marking the period when their daughter Lisa Marie was born. After significant renovations, the property was sold in 2019 for an impressive $25.5 million, showcasing the lasting allure of celebrity residences and the historic value they carry.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: Michael Douglas keeps 190-acre Mallorca estate 36 years after buying it
item.description: Michael Douglas and Catherine Zeta-Jones enjoy their historic estate, S'Estaca, located in Mallorca. The property, set on 190 acres, features multiple buildings and stunning views of the Mediterranean Sea. Douglas originally purchased the estate in 1990 with his first wife, Diandra Luker, and they later became the sole owners. The couple has created cherished family memories there, raising their two children while entertaining numerous famous guests.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Michael Dell loses $20 billion in one day after Barclays downgrade
item.description: Michael Dell experienced a substantial decline in net worth, dropping more than $20 billion in just one day. This decline was prompted by a major decrease in his company's stock value following an analyst downgrade. Earlier this year, Dell's net worth had notably increased, bringing him closer to the highest billionaires in the world.

item.title: No more guessing who's calling! Govt mandates caller ID display from Nov 1
item.description: The Department of Telecommunications is preparing to roll out Calling Name Presentation, a feature that shows the caller's name in addition to their number on the recipient's screen. This functionality will first be implemented on 4G networks before extending to other versions. Users will have the choice to opt-out if they utilize the calling line identification restriction service, striking a balance between enhancing caller recognition and safeguarding data privacy.
item.dc:creator: SHIVANGHI PAYAL

item.title: Ex-IAS Divya launches party: 10 civil servants who quit service to enter politics
item.description: Divya Mittal, an ex-IAS officer, has established the Jan Neeti Bharat party in preparation for the forthcoming elections. With a focus on enhancing citizen participation in policymaking rather than adhering to conventional governance methods, she aims to make a significant impact. Her decision to retire after 13 years in civil service aligns with a trend of bureaucrats entering politics.
item.dc:creator: PALLAVI

item.title: 6,000 cops, 200 CAPF companies, 21 roads facing curbs: Delhi gears up for CJP march
item.description: Central Delhi is preparing for a significant security operation ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's proposed march. The Delhi Police will deploy around 6,000 personnel and implement traffic restrictions in the area. The Central Park at Connaught Place is set to remain closed, impacting the proposed gathering. Authorities have denotified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, redirecting protests to alternative venues.
item.dc:creator: TOI CITY DESK

item.title: From Ambani to Zelenskyy, Musk mixes business with politics
item.description: Elon Musk is increasingly acting as an influential figure in global politics and domestic affairs. His recent remarks about Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reflect attempts to sway leadership in Ukraine. Musk's substantial financial contributions to American politics emphasize his growing influence over legislative decisions. His disputes with India regarding Starlink highlight the intersection of business interests and political power.
item.dc:creator: CHIDANAND RAJGHATTA

item.title: 'Will stand with Pak if US attacks': Rajasthan BJP chief’s remark sparks outcry
item.description: Rajasthan BJP president Madan Rathore stated that India would align with Pakistan in a potential US-Pakistan conflict. This statement has drawn significant criticism from Congress leaders, including Shama Mohamed. Mohamed questioned the BJP's stance and asked for clarification from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. Rathore also accused Rahul Gandhi of inciting unrest and mentioned foreign interference in India's stability.
item.dc:creator: PALLAVI

item.title: Imran Khan asked to leave India: What rights do OCI cardholders have?
item.description: Actor Imran Khan faces deportation from India by October 28 due to his involvement in a protest. This action stems from a complaint lodged by BJP leader Kirit Somaiya regarding legal violations during the demonstration. Khan, a US citizen and OCI cardholder, was detained at the protest site in Mumbai. His participation raises questions about the rights of foreign nationals involved in political activities.

item.title: Brazil plants 840,000 trees to restore 607 hectares of Atlantic Forest
item.description: Brazil's Atlantic Forest is undergoing remarkable restoration efforts, spearheaded by World Land Trust and Reserva Ecológica de Guapiaçu. With 840,000 trees planted over 20 years, 607 hectares of degraded land have been revived into verdant forest. This initiative has created a vital wildlife corridor, facilitating the return of over 220 bird species to the previous wetland, while striving to protect and enhance the Guapiaçu watershed's remaining forest.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Yemen claims over 700 Houthis killed after 1,250 strikes rained within 24 hours
item.description: Yemen armed forces reported conducting 1,250 targeting operations against Houthis in one day. These strikes coincided with Houthi attacks on Aden’s presidential palace, resulting in casualties. Houthi spokesperson denied claims of missile strikes towards Medina, asserting their innocence. Meanwhile, the Saudi-led coalition intercepted several missiles aimed at its territories amid ongoing tensions. Overall, hostilities between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia have intensified over recent months.
item.dc:creator: PRANJAL PANDEY

item.title: ‘Collapse could be precipitous’: Super El Niño could push coral reefs to extinction
item.description: Researchers warn that the ongoing super El Niño could further endanger already vulnerable coral species. The rise in ocean temperatures has led to record coral bleaching events which have severe consequences for coral health. Nearly half of coral species were at increased risk of extinction by 2020 due to climate change effects. Future coral assessments may reveal even more alarming data regarding extinction risks among coral species.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: India’s current account deficit narrows to $5.2 billion in August, RBI data shows
item.description: India's overall balance of payments showed a surplus of $45.4 billion in August 2026. This significant surplus is attributed to an increase in foreign currency inflows, especially from non-resident Indian deposits. The current account deficit also narrowed slightly to $5.2 billion during the same month. Foreign direct investment improved, with net inflows of $3.3 billion recorded.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: 'Skipped dinner, wept': 'Blue drum' murder convicts' 1st night in jail
item.description: Muskan Rastogi and Sahil Shukla spent a troubled first night in jail after receiving a death sentence. They were convicted for the brutal murder of Muskan's husband, Saurabh Rajput, earlier this year. The court described the murder as extremely cruel and grave, leading to their sentencing. Muskan is allowed to keep her infant daughter Radha with her while seeking permission to meet her elder daughter, Pihu.

item.title: Andhra Pradesh shocker: Lover lured to pond, beaten to death; husband, wife arrested
item.description: Mamidi Gouri Shankar and his wife, Mamidi Lakshmi Durga, are accused of orchestrating Thumula Lakshmana's murder. Lakshmana allegedly had an extramarital affair with Lakshmi Durga, leading to disputes with her husband. Following a planned attack, he was murdered and his body dumped in a canal. Police arrested several individuals linked to the crime, including the couple, as the investigation progressed.
